name: Maxwell Park Campground
note: City of Arlington in-town campground in Maxwell Park, the block between Elm St (US 14) and the railroad at N Main St downtown, with a free grass tent area; the city's other campground, Nordland Park, is about 0.45 km SE. No season or booking method is published (a 2020 camper review says to pay at the city office, 202 W Elm St, with an after-hours drop box): call the city to confirm. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: City of Arlington camping page (cityofarlingtonsd.com/camping, read 2026-11-22, (c) 2026): 'The City of Arlington maintains two campgrounds inside the city limits... Maxwell Park Campground | 101 North Main Street | This campground is convenient to all downtown activities. There are 4 camper pads located in Maxwell Park (1-50 amp pad and 3-30 amp pads). There is also grass area for tent campers at no charge. There is a $10.00/night charge for the electricity and a camper dump station', city office (605) 983-5251 -> a city campground named on the town's own current page (public ladder step 1; local: no price gate or presence rule). Located on Esri Wayback imagery (2023-05-01 WV02 z18/z19, 2022-09-14 and 2021-04-24 WV02 z19): the block NW of the Elm St / N Main St corner, with a gravel drive curving through it from the NW side street to a gravel area by a small building on the Main St side, a tree/shrub row along Elm St, and a travel trailer about 13 m long parked on the gravel beside the drive in both 2021 and 2022 -> drive-in pads off paved town streets that fit a 23-ft rig. No 4WD, road, horse or long-stay wording anywhere. The Dyrt lists it (municipal; 1 review, 2020-09: electric sites, shade, shrub row between campers and the road, pay at the municipal building with an after-hours drop box); RV Life does not list it (Algolia, 5 km around the pin, 2026-11-22: only Nordland Park 12654).
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-22: Esri World Imagery (town frame 44.3570-44.3710, -97.1440--97.1240, rendered; current 2025-07 capture is partly cloud-covered) and Esri Wayback 2023-05-01 z18/z19, 2022-09-14 z19, 2021-04-24 z19 at 44.3645-44.3650,-97.1342--97.1335 (all rendered). The campground is a downtown block bounded by Elm St (US 14), N Main St, a side street and the railroad/grain-elevator yard; no water in or beside it. The nearest water is Lake Arlington, a ~4-acre town pond south of US 14 about 0.45-0.5 km SE (by Nordland Park, 5836), out of sight behind the highway and town blocks -> not waterfront.

fees.note: City of Arlington: electricity $10 a night; non-electric use and the grass tent area are free.

fees_source: https://cityofarlingtonsd.com/camping ('Both are free for non-electrical spots but if electricity is needed the cost is just $10.00 per night'; Maxwell Park: 'grass area for tent campers at no charge. There is a $10.00/night charge for the electricity'), read 2026-11-22. Stored 0/10 by the schema's free-beside-priced rule, matching 5836 Nordland Park on the same page.

hookups.note: One 50 A pad and three 30 A pads.

hookups_source: https://cityofarlingtonsd.com/camping ('4 camper pads located in Maxwell Park (1-50 amp pad and 3-30 amp pads)'), read 2026-11-22; water and sewer at the sites are not mentioned, so left absent

facilities_source: https://cityofarlingtonsd.com/camping (Maxwell Park: '...a $10.00/night charge for the electricity and a camper dump station'), read 2026-11-22; restrooms, showers and water not mentioned
rvlife: not listed (RV Life Algolia park index, 5 km around the pin, 2026-11-22: only Nordland Park Campground 12654)
curation_note: SD lead 1 (found p3-568 at 5836 Nordland Park; vetted 2026-11-22): separate city campground on the same City of Arlington page, ~0.45 km NW of 5836 across US 14, with its own pads, hookups and dump station. Pin is my imagery read of the gravel area where a trailer is parked in 2021 and 2022 captures, not from a published map. --Claude
flags: Not a duplicate: the only DB entry within 14 km is 5836 Nordland Park Campground (44.36150,-97.13040), 0.45 km SE, which the city page describes separately ('Nordland Park Campground ... north side of Lake Arlington on Highways 14 & 81', 5 pads). Both are city-run with one pay route, but each has its own pads and entrance; under the 1 km split rule these would not be split from one entry, but they were never one entry.

Pin: The Dyrt's point (44.36500,-97.13400, an address geocode) is ~30 m NW of the pin, in the same block; the pin is on the gravel beside the drive where a ~13 m travel trailer stood in the 2021-04 and 2022-09 Wayback captures. The four pads are not individually distinguishable on imagery and no city map exists.

Thin evidence beyond the city page: no Google check was run (not required on public ladder step 1), RV Life does not list it, and the only camper review is from 2020. Season and payment method are unpublished; the note says to call the city.
Pad length unstated by the city; the ~13 m rig parked there in two captures is the basis for the 23-ft fit.
